2026_346_3c_draft_boe_tsd_athletic_handb.paragraph: A draft Troy School District Athletic Handbook for Students, revised Spring 2026, presented to the Board as agenda item 3C. Fifteen sections set out eligibility rules, awards, amateur status, attendance, season expectations including the TROY CAP PACT, transportation, uniforms, substance policy, summer programs, name-image-likeness rules, supplemental team rules, a four-level disciplinary framework, and appeal procedures, all layered under the Troy School District Student Code of Conduct and MHSAA regulations. A central change is a percentage-based suspension framework tying Level I through Level IV violations to consequences ranging from no suspension to removal from the team for 50-100% of the season.
2026_346_3c_draft_boe_tsd_athletic_handb.page:
**What it is**
Draft Troy School District Athletic Handbook for Students, revised Spring 2026, submitted to the Board of Education as item 3C. It integrates Michigan High School Athletic Association (MHSAA) rules as adopted by the district with district-specific interscholastic athletic policies, and operates under the Troy School District Student Code of Conduct, which takes precedence in any conflict. Policies marked with an asterisk are district-adopted policies that also align with MHSAA regulations. The handbook is in effect all year.

**Section I - Eligibility**
Enrollment by the Monday of the fourth week of the semester; TCCHS and IA East students participate at their home school by residency. High school participants must be under 19, with a nineteenth birthday on or after September 1 preserving eligibility for the balance of the year; seventh and eighth graders must be under 14 and 15 respectively. FinalForms is the district's digital athletic clearance platform, requiring parent and student accounts, electronic forms, a physical dated after April 15 of the previous school year completed by an M.D., D.O., physician assistant or nurse practitioner, and a health history; required acknowledgements include the Athletic Handbook, CAP PACT Agreement, Application to Participate, Pay to Participate Agreement (paid before the first competition), Athletics Transportation Agreement, Concussion Awareness form, and MHSAA Acknowledgement of Risk. Paper submissions are no longer accepted. MHSAA allows no more than four seasons of competition per sport in grades 9-12, across four first semesters and four second semesters.

**Academic eligibility**
Passing credit in a minimum of five classes in the previous semester is required. Building-specific standards: Troy College and Career High School, 7 of 8 classes over the previous two semesters; Intersect and Inspire High School, 5 of 6 over the previous two semesters; International Academy, 7 of 8 in the previous semester; middle school, 5 of 6 in the previous quarter. Eligibility is reviewed at the end of each marking period (every 10 weeks), with reinstatement by weekly progress report and a minimum ineligibility period of one full calendar week (Monday through Sunday). Prior-semester deficiencies carry a minimum of 60 scheduled school days of ineligibility. New transfer students get one transitional semester at the MHSAA minimum of four passing classes.

**Sections II-XIII**
Awards may not exceed a fair market value of $25.00, with cash, certificates and negotiable documents prohibited; violations bring at least one semester of ineligibility. Amateur status bars pay for participation, paid officiating of interscholastic contests, and professional contracts, with reinstatement requests to the MHSAA only after one full school year. Outside-of-school competition in the same sport during the season brings a minimum of two contests of ineligibility at middle school and three at high school. Full-day school attendance is required to participate. Transportation with the team is required, with departures only to a parent, legal guardian, or adult family member with prior FinalForms permission and coach approval. Uniform and equipment loss makes the athlete financially responsible.

**Substance policy**
High school violations are cumulative across a student's career. First tobacco/nicotine violation: minimum 1 contest or 1 week, not to exceed 10% of the regular season. First alcohol/drug or second tobacco violation: minimum 2 contests or 2 weeks, not to exceed 20%. Second alcohol/drug or third tobacco: removal for the season, and if less than 50% of the season remains, ineligibility for the first 50% of the next season. Third alcohol/drug or fourth tobacco: 365-day suspension. Fourth alcohol/drug or fifth tobacco: permanent loss of eligibility. Middle school violators are immediately removed from the team.

**Sections XIV-XV**
A four-level disciplinary framework pairs violation levels with baseline consequences: Level I, no suspension (0%, coach-managed); Level II, 10-20% of contests; Level III, 20-40% of contests and at least MHSAA minimums; Level IV, removal from the team for 50-100% of the season. Appeals go in writing to the building principal or athletic coordinator within five school days, with a meeting within two school days and a written decision within two school days, then to the district Director of Athletics within two school days. MHSAA eligibility and transfer appeals follow a separate MHSAA process whose decisions are final and binding.
2026_346_3c_draft_boe_tsd_athletic_handb.verbose:
**Document and framing**
The draft Athletic Handbook for Students, revised Spring 2026, was presented to the Troy School District Board of Education as agenda item 3C on April 7, 2026. It is organized into a table of contents and fifteen numbered sections spanning pages 1 through 27, covering eligibility, awards, amateur status, outside competition, school attendance, practice and contest attendance, season expectations and the TROY CAP PACT, travel, uniforms and equipment, substance use, summer and off-season programs, name-image-likeness, supplemental rules, a disciplinary framework, and appeal procedures.

**Introduction**
The handbook provides a consistent framework of expectations for all student-athletes regardless of team or school, integrating Michigan High School Athletic Association (MHSAA) rules as adopted by Troy School District with district-specific policies. Athletics are described as a vital extension of the classroom developing social-emotional learning, personal responsibility, teamwork, leadership, time management, and athletic skill. The handbook operates under the umbrella of the Troy School District Student Code of Conduct, so a student-athlete violating the Code is also subject to the handbook's disciplinary procedures. The handbook is in effect throughout the entire year. An academically ineligible student may still practice with the team provided they are not under school suspension, though inability to compete may affect eligibility for athletic awards under team-specific requirements set by the coach. Policies marked with an asterisk are district-adopted policies that also align with MHSAA regulations.

**Section I - Rules of Eligibility for Participation**
Enrollment: the student must be enrolled by the Monday of the fourth week of the semester in which they compete, must reside in the school boundaries of the school attended, and must be enrolled in the school for which they compete. Student-athletes attending TCCHS and IA East must participate in athletics at their home school based on residency.

Age: high school students in grades nine through twelve must be under nineteen (19) years of age; a nineteenth birthday occurring on or after September 1 of the current school year preserves eligibility for the balance of the school year. Seventh and eighth grade students must be under fourteen (14) and fifteen (15) years of age respectively, with the same September 1 rule.

FinalForms: all parents/guardians and student-athletes must complete athletic registration through FinalForms, the district's designated digital platform for athletic clearance, including a fully completed parent account and student account, all electronic forms and agreements, a current physical form dated after April 15 of the previous school year, and a completed health history and medical profile. Required acknowledgements are the Athletic Handbook for Student-Athletes, the CAP PACT Agreement form (completed prior to the start of the season), the Application to Participate form, the Pay to Participate Agreement (paid before the first competition), the Athletics Transportation Agreement form, the Concussion Awareness form, and the MHSAA Acknowledgement of Risk form. Forms are stored in FinalForms and accessible to coaches, athletic trainers, the building athletic coordinator, and the district athletic director. Paper submissions are no longer accepted unless directed by the athletic department.

Physical examination: must be completed by a physician (M.D. or D.O.), physician assistant, or nurse practitioner, dated on or after April 15 of the previous school year, and submitted electronically via FinalForms before any tryouts, practices, or contests.

Seasons of competition: no more than four (4) seasons of interscholastic competition in a specific sport in grades 9 through 12, distributed as no more than four first semesters and four second semesters. A student may not participate in more than one season per sport per school year even where the sport is offered twice, such as bowling or tennis. Fall sideline cheer is not a competition season and does not count as an additional season alongside winter competitive cheer. Grades 7 and 8 are not limited in number of seasons.

Semester of eligibility: no eligibility after enrollment in grades 9 through 12 for more than four first semesters and four second semesters. Enrollment by the Monday of the fourth week of a semester, or participation in one or more contests, constitutes a full semester of eligibility. Semesters in which an eligible student chooses not to participate still count. Grades 7 and 8 are unlimited, but once a student enters 9th grade semesters must be consecutive.

Academic eligibility: passing grades (credit) in a minimum of five (5) classes in the previous semester. Troy College and Career High School students must pass at least 7 of 8 classes during the previous two semesters; Intersect and Inspire High School students at least 5 of 6 during the previous two semesters; International Academy at least 7 of 8 during the previous semester; middle school students 5 of 6 during the previous quarter. Ineligibility based on prior-semester final grades lasts the complete following semester unless the MHSAA 60-Day Rule applies. Eligibility is formally reviewed at the end of each marking period, every 10 weeks; a student failing a quarterly grade check becomes ineligible for competition and may regain eligibility with a weekly academic progress report, with the ineligibility period no less than one full calendar week, Monday through Sunday. Deficiencies from the previous semester bring a minimum of sixty (60) scheduled school days of ineligibility in the current semester or until eligibility is restored. New transfer students receive one semester to meet district requirements and must meet the MHSAA minimum of passing four (4) classes during that transitional semester. Middle school students must pass at least five of six classes each marking period, with weekly progress monitoring otherwise.

**Section II - Awards**
Consistent with MHSAA guidelines, a student-athlete may accept a symbolic or merchandise award not exceeding a fair market value of twenty-five dollars ($25.00). Permitted are banquets, luncheons and dinners, non-competitive trips, and spectator admission to non-Troy School District events accepted in kind. Prohibited are cash, merchandise certificates or negotiable financial documents, and memberships, privileges, services, athletic equipment, apparel, or accessories/jewelry exceeding the $25 limit. No individual, including a parent, relative, or friend, may accept an award on behalf of the student-athlete prior to high school graduation. Violation brings ineligibility for at least one semester from the date of violation; if the violation occurs after the fourth Monday of a semester, ineligibility runs for the remainder of that semester and the entire next semester.

**Section III - Maintaining Amateur Status**
Student-athletes may not accept money or other valuable consideration for participating in athletics, sports, or games (separate from permissible NIL activities), may not receive compensation for officiating interscholastic contests, and may not sign a contract or agreement to play or try out with a professional team. The rule applies to MHSAA-sponsored sports: Baseball, Basketball, Cross Country, Football, Golf, Gymnastics, Soccer, Softball, Skiing, Tennis, Track & Field, Volleyball, Wrestling, Ice Hockey, Competitive Cheer, and Swimming & Diving. Instructional fees or payment for coaching youth or recreational sports may be allowed if unconnected to interscholastic athletics. A violator may not apply for reinstatement until one full school year has passed, after which a formal request may be submitted to the MHSAA.

**Section IV - Outside of School Athletic Competition**
Once a student participates in any practice, tryout, scrimmage, or contest on a school team, they may not participate in non-school (club, AAU, travel, rec) competition in the same sport during that season without penalty. Middle school violators are ineligible for a minimum of the next two (2) school contests or dates of competition; high school violators for a minimum of the next three (3), and ineligibility may extend to the remainder of the season. Under MHSAA rules tryouts count as practice. The Limited Team Membership provision sets a minimum of the next three (3) days of competition and a maximum of the remainder of that sport season. Students may not participate in any "all-star" contests in an MHSAA-sponsored sport during the school year. These rules reflect Section 12(A) - Limited Team Membership of the MHSAA handbook.

**Section V - Student Attendance Required for Athletics**
A student must be in school for the full instructional day to participate in practice, scrimmage, or competition that day. Acceptable excused absences include illness with documentation, medical or dental appointments with verification, court appearances, religious observances, bereavement or family emergencies, and pre-approved college visits or academic travel; extenuating circumstances may be approved by the building principal or designee. Unexcused absences (skipping, oversleeping, leaving campus without permission, failure to document) make a student ineligible that day, and participating anyway is a Code of Conduct violation subject to discipline determined by the coach, athletic coordinator, and building administrator.

**Section VI - Attendance at Practices and Contests**
Excused absences include illness or injury, required school-related activities, family emergencies or pre-approved commitments, religious holidays and cultural observances (automatically excused without penalty when the coach is notified in advance), and school vacation periods with school-sponsored or parent-approved trips. Unexcused absences include failure to attend without prior communication, leaving early or arriving late without approval, and missing practice for non-essential personal activities; consequences may include reduced playing time, loss of leadership roles, and team consequences in supplemental rules. Level-based expectations are set for Middle School (grades 7-8), Freshman level (primarily 9th grade), Junior Varsity (JV/JVA), and Varsity, escalating from regular attendance and communication toward full commitment, with all four levels stating that cultural and religious observances are honored without penalty when communicated timely.

**Section VII - Season Expectations and the TROY CAP PACT**
Philosophies and coach, player, and parent expectations are defined for Middle School (skill development, teamwork, playing time for all when possible, emphasis on teaching over winning), Freshman / JV B (merit-based playing time begins, shift from "equal play" to "earned play"), Junior Varsity / JVA covering 9th-11th grades (advanced tactics, varsity readiness evaluation), and Varsity (competitive excellence, strategic decisions that may limit playing time). The TROY CAP PACT (Coach-Athlete-Parent PACT) must be reviewed and signed by all student-athletes, parents, and coaches prior to each season through FinalForms, and enumerates each constituent's expectations of the others, including nine coach expectations of parents, six parent expectations of coach, fourteen coach expectations of athlete, ten athlete expectations of coach, and six athlete expectations of parents.

Complaint/Grievance Policy: the athlete first talks with the coach; informally, the parent then calls or emails the coach and allows two (2) school days for a response and possible face-to-face meeting with parent, athlete, and coach. Level 1 requires written concerns to the coach with a written reply within five (5) school days. Level 2 requires written disagreement to the building Athletic Coordinator within five (5) school days with the Level 1 response attached; the Athletic Coordinator conducts an independent investigation and sends a written reply within seven (7) school days. Level 3 is a meeting with the Building Principal and District Athletic Director. Complaints alleging a potential criminal act or immoral behavior by a coach begin in writing at Level 2.

**Section VIII - Traveling to and from Away Contests**
Athletes are expected to travel with the team when district transportation is provided, using school-owned, chartered, or approved vehicles. Under the FinalForms Transportation Agreement, students may leave a contest site with a parent, legal guardian, or adult family member only with prior written permission through FinalForms and advance coach approval. Where district transportation is not used, the coach must document departure through a signed sign-out form or approved sign-off list. First violation: ineligible for the next scheduled contest, may continue practicing. Second violation: possible removal from the team for the remainder of the season.

**Section IX - Uniforms and Equipment**
Items must be used only for school-sanctioned practices and competitions, returned clean and in good condition, and stored securely. Athletes are financially responsible for lost, abused, damaged, or unreturned items; until replacement cost is resolved, participation in future seasons is suspended and awards, letters, or recognitions may be withheld.

**Section X - Tobacco, Alcohol and Other Drug Substances**
Prohibited at all times, on and off school grounds, year-round: tobacco/nicotine products including vaping devices; alcohol; marijuana, non-prescribed controlled substances, or look-alike substances; banned performance-enhancing drugs or supplements as defined by the NCAA and Michigan Department of Health; prescription medication not prescribed to the student; and misuse of over-the-counter medication. Legally prescribed medication used as directed is not a violation. Middle school violators are immediately removed from their team, with reinstatement considered only after a meeting involving the student, parent/guardian, and building administrator. High school violations are cumulative from the first day of participation as a freshman, and the student must complete the season in good standing for missed contests to count toward the consequence. In-season violations apply immediately to the current sport; out-of-season violations are enforced at the beginning of the next season of participation, even in the next school year. First tobacco/nicotine violation: minimum 1 contest or 1 week suspension, whichever is greater, not to exceed 10% of the regular season, with an optional educational workshop at family cost and possible parent conference. First alcohol/drug or second tobacco violation: minimum 2 contests or 2 weeks, not to exceed 20% of the regular season, mandatory parent meeting with coach and building administrator, required substance education or intervention program at family cost, with end-of-season missed games carrying over. Second alcohol/drug or third tobacco: immediate removal for the current season, and if less than 50% of the season remains, ineligibility for the first 50% of the next season, plus a required professional assessment from a Michigan Department of Health-approved provider at family cost. Third alcohol/drug or fourth tobacco: suspension from all athletic participation for 365 days from the date of the confirmed violation. Fourth alcohol/drug or fifth tobacco: permanent loss of athletic eligibility in the Troy School District.

**Section XI - Summer and Off-Season Programs**
Participation is strictly voluntary. Per MHSAA regulations, students may not be required to attend non-school-sponsored off-season activity as a condition of making a team, earning a roster spot, receiving playing time, or being placed at a particular level such as JV or Varsity. Coaches must communicate that no negative consequences follow from choosing not to participate.

**Section XII - Name, Image, and Likeness (NIL) / Personal Branding Activities (PBA)**
NIL/PBA is permitted in accordance with MHSAA regulations provided activities are independent of school teams and programs, compensation is not tied to athletic performance, participation, or team success, activities occur outside school time and away from school-sponsored events and facilities, and the activity complies with MHSAA rules, district policies, and law. Prohibited: use of school names, logos, uniforms, mascots or facilities; implying school, district, or MHSAA endorsement; NIL activity during school hours, practices, contests, or team events; pay-for-play compensation; agreements arranged by coaches, school personnel, or booster organizations; collectives or group NIL agreements; and promotion of products or services violating school policies or MHSAA standards. Agreements must be reported per MHSAA requirements prior to participation; the district, coaches, and staff do not provide legal, tax, or contract guidance. NIL may not be used to influence enrollment, transfer decisions, or team placement, and MHSAA transfer and undue influence rules remain in effect.

**Section XIII - Supplemental Rules and Regulations**
Sport-specific supplemental rules may be developed by coaches and must be approved by the building athletic coordinator and building principal or designee; athlete-specific plans or behavior contracts require approval by the building athletic coordinator or Director of Athletics. Supplemental rules must be in writing and distributed at the start of the season and typically define attitude, effort, attendance, cooperation, team standards, and varsity letter criteria. A student suspended from school is ineligible for any practices or contests during the suspension; an academically ineligible student may practice at the coach's discretion but may not compete; a student dismissed for the remainder of a season forfeits eligibility for team awards or varsity letters for that season.

**Section XIV - Disciplinary Framework**
Discipline is progressive, educational, and restorative when appropriate, aligned with MHSAA and National Federation of State High School Associations (NFHS) standards, with the Troy School District Code of Conduct governing and superseding the handbook in any conflict. Level I minor violations (tardiness, unexcused practice absence, dress code, non-directed inappropriate language, failure to follow team procedures) draw verbal warnings, parent communication, temporary reduced playing time, team consequences, and restorative conversation. Level II moderate violations (repeated Level I, disrespect, minor unsportsmanlike conduct, social media misuse, minor school infractions) draw suspension from contests of 1-3 or a defined percentage, parent conference, behavioral contract, removal from leadership roles, and a restorative meeting. Level III major violations (insubordination, ejection per MHSAA/NFHS rules, bullying, harassment or hazing, substance use/possession, academic dishonesty affecting eligibility, significant school violations) draw multi-contest suspension aligned with MHSAA minimums, temporary removal from team activities, mandatory parent conference, educational interventions, probationary status, and a structured restorative process. Level IV severe violations (fighting, hazing, theft, vandalism or criminal behavior, distribution of controlled substances, serious harassment, discrimination or threats, egregious or repeated major violations) draw immediate suspension, removal from the team for the remainder of the season or longer, referral to school and/or legal authorities, and loss of awards, honors, and leadership roles. Due process affords clear communication of the violation, an opportunity to respond, review by coach and/or athletic administration, and parent notification for Levels II-IV. The Athletic Director has final authority on athletic eligibility decisions. Suspension from the school day results in ineligibility for all after-school athletic activities that day, tryout-period suspensions may affect team selection, and athletic suspensions may carry over between seasons and into the next school year. The percentage-based suspension framework sets Level I at no suspension, 0%, coach-managed; Level II short-term suspension at 10-20% of contests, typically 1 contest; Level III significant suspension at 20-40% of contests, meeting or exceeding MHSAA minimums for ejections; and Level IV removal from team at 50-100% of the season, possibly a full-season suspension.

**Section XV - Appeal Procedures**
A student-athlete found in violation of Sections V-XII may appeal, consistent with the Troy School District Student Code of Conduct. The appeal must be initiated in writing to the building principal and/or building athletic coordinator within five (5) school days of the disciplinary action being communicated. A meeting including the student, the coach, and possibly the parent/guardian is convened within two (2) school days, and a written decision upholding, modifying, or revoking the action is issued within two (2) school days. Further appeal goes in writing to the district Director of Athletics within two (2) school days of the building-level decision. Appeals about eligibility, transfer rules, or MHSAA violations are submitted through the school athletic coordinator or district director of athletics to the MHSAA, follow a separate process, and MHSAA decisions are final and binding at the state level.

2026_347_march_2026_spring_update.paragraph: A March 9, 2026 memorandum from MJ School Policy Services to MJ Policy Service Clients transmitting the March 2026 policy manual and administrative regulations update. Nine numbered revisions, Update 22.01 through Update 22.09, are proposed across the Students, Curriculum and Instruction, Business, Facilities and Operations, School and Community Relations, and General Policies series, with no changes recommended for the Introduction, Bylaws, or Personnel series. The most consequential item is Update 22.03, which implements MCL 380.1303a, added by House Bill 4141 and Senate Bill 495 signed February 10, 2026, requiring boards to prohibit student wireless communication device use during instructional time effective for the 2026-27 school year.
2026_347_march_2026_spring_update.page:
**What it is**
Memorandum dated March 9, 2026 from MJ School Policy Services to MJ Policy Service Clients regarding the Policy Manual and Administrative Regulations Update - March 2026. Revisions are presented by section with an individual update number (e.g., Update 22.01) and a narrative basis. Additions are shown in red, deletions in blue, and areas highlighted in yellow require additional information from the district. Questions go to Policy@MillerJohnson.com.

**Sections with no recommended updates**
Introduction - 0000 Series; Bylaws - 1000 Series; Personnel - 4000 Series.

**Students - 2000 Series**
- Update 22.01 (Policy 2003, Education Records): the fiscal year 2026 State School Aid Act includes MCL 388.1764k, adding requirements for districts and intermediate school districts regarding student surveys. Revised language preserves parental inspection rights and consent requirements for surveys funded by the U.S. Department of Education covering political or religious affiliations, mental or psychological problems, sexual behavior or attitudes, illegal or self-incriminating behavior, critical appraisals of close relations, privileged relationships with lawyers, physicians and ministers, and income. Under MCL 388.1764k the district must post questions and results of district-wide, state or federally mandated, and grade-level-wide surveys on its website and notify parents, subject to FERPA before releasing results.
- Update 22.02 (Policy 2004, Extracurricular Activities): applies to MHSAA member districts. The MHSAA approved expansion of its personal branding activities (PBA) / name, image, or likeness (NIL) rule, Regulation I, Section 11 C - Amateur Status/Awards, on January 23, 2026, effective immediately, allowing compensation for PBA regardless of whether it relates to athletics. New policy language prohibits PBA/NIL agreements that violate Board Policy or the Student Code of Conduct and bars such activities during school hours or events or on district property without prior written Superintendent approval.
- Update 22.03 (Policy 2006, Behavior): Governor Whitmer signed House Bill 4141 and Senate Bill 495 on February 10, 2026, amending the Revised School Code at MCL 380.1303a to require boards to adopt a policy prohibiting wireless communications device use during instructional time, effective for the 2026-27 school year. Devices must be turned off and kept out of sight in lockers or cubbies. Exemptions cover medically necessary devices, district-owned or issued devices, instructional-purpose devices, special education programming or accommodations under a Section 504 Plan, IEP, or the ADA, lesson-specific academic assignments, and emergency situations under the district's Emergency Operations Plan pursuant to MCL 380.1308b. Recording or broadcasting others requires permission, excluding activities where personal recording is generally permitted such as athletic events and arts performances.

**Curriculum and Instruction - 3000 Series**
- Update 22.04 (Policy 3003, Instruction): under MCL 388.1764k, the district must notify parents by September 30, 2026 if it uses a K-5 curriculum not on the state's evidence-based list under MCL 380.1280f.

**Business - 5000 Series**
- Update 22.05 (Policy 5003, Purchasing): corrects a minor spelling/grammatical error, replacing "statuses" with "statutes" in the internal control language for state/federal grants and awards.

**Facilities and Operations - 6000 Series**
- Update 22.06 (Policy 6013, Facility Dog): clarifies that a facility dog is a School District owned dog trained to work within school facilities and at school events.

**School and Community Relations - 7000 Series**
- Update 22.07 (Policy 7001, Goal): adds a Record Retention section referencing the Michigan Department of Technology, Management & Budget retention schedule for school districts.
- Update 22.08 (Policy 7008, Advertising): gives districts more flexibility in preparing regulations on accepting advertisements.

**General Policies - 8000 Series**
- Update 22.09 (Policy 8003, Website and Digital Content Accessibility): conforms the policy to WCAG 2.1 Level AA per updated U.S. Department of Justice requirements, with periodic accessibility audits of the website, online platforms, and mobile applications.
2026_347_march_2026_spring_update.verbose:
**Memorandum header**
TO: MJ Policy Service Clients. FROM: MJ School Policy Services. DATE: March 9, 2026. RE: Policy Manual and Administrative Regulations Update - March 2026. The memo transmits substantive updates to all MJ School Policy Services policy and administrative regulations manuals. Proposed revisions are presented by section with a specific update number for ease of reference, along with a narrative providing the basis for the contemplated modification. All updates are numbered individually (i.e., Update 22.01). Additions to policy or administrative regulation language are shown in red; deletions are shown in blue; areas highlighted in yellow require additional information from the district to complete the update. Because each district manual is unique and modified consistent with district priority and prerogative, recommended modifications may already be contained in completed manuals. Questions about how the revisions fit existing manuals go to Policy@MillerJohnson.com, and districts behind on policy updates are urged to contact the office for compliance support.

**Sections with no recommended policy updates**
Introduction - 0000 Series, Bylaws - 1000 Series, and Personnel - 4000 Series each carry the statement that there are no recommended policy updates.

**Update 22.01 - Policy 2003, Education Records (Students - 2000 Series)**
The fiscal year 2026 State School Aid Act includes MCL 388.1764k, which provides additional requirements for school districts and intermediate school districts regarding student surveys. Adoption of the revisions is recommended to ensure compliance with Section 164k. Miller Johnson previously issued guidance titled "New Compliance Requirements Under Section 164k - State School Aid Act (FY 2025-2026)" and "Additional Guidance on Section 164k Compliance - District Surveys & Curriculum Requirements."

The revised Student Surveys language states that, consistent with applicable law, parents may inspect all materials used for any student survey, analysis, or evaluation conducted by the School District in connection with a program funded by the United States Department of Education. Without parental consent, the district will not require a student to participate in such a survey, analysis, or evaluation that reveals or is intended to reveal information concerning the student or the student's parents' political or religious affiliations, beliefs, or practices; mental or psychological problems; sexual behavior or attitudes; illegal, anti-social, self-incriminating, or demeaning behavior; critical appraisals of other individuals with whom the student or the student's parents have close family relationships; legally recognized privileged or analogous relationships such as those with lawyers, physicians, and ministers; or income, other than when required by law to determine eligibility for programs or financial assistance.

New language adds that, in compliance with MCL 388.1764k, the School District will ensure that questions and results of District-wide surveys, state or federally mandated surveys, and surveys distributed to all students in a grade level are made available to the public by being posted on the District's website, and that parents will be notified of these survey questions and results. The District will comply with the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act ("FERPA") before releasing any survey results.

**Update 22.02 - Policy 2004, Extracurricular Activities (Students - 2000 Series)**
This update applies to school districts that are members of the Michigan High School Athletic Association ("MHSAA"). The MHSAA approved an expansion of its personal branding activities ("PBA") / name, image, or likeness ("NIL") rule - Regulation I, Section 11 C - Amateur Status/Awards on January 23, 2026. Effective immediately, a student may earn compensation through their PBA (use of their NIL), such as promoting or endorsing a product or service, regardless of whether the PBA relates to athletics. Because students may now engage in PBA/NIL agreements, the additional policy language is intended to prohibit students from entering agreements that violate Board Policy and/or the Student Code of Conduct and to provide additional protections for the school district.

The Athletics section of the policy states that the Superintendent, in consultation with the Board and selected School District personnel, will develop and administer a robust program of interscholastic athletics, adhering at all times to the principle that participants are students first and athletes second. In addition to MHSAA regulations and limitations, the School District prohibits students from engaging in personal branding activities / name, image, or likeness agreements that violate Board Policy or the Student Code of Conduct, and students may be disciplined under Board Policy and/or the Student Code of Conduct for such violations. PBA/NIL activities shall not occur during school hours or events or on School District property unless prior written approval is provided by the Superintendent.

**Update 22.03 - Policy 2006, Behavior (Students - 2000 Series)**
Governor Whitmer signed House Bill 4141 and Senate Bill 495 on February 10, 2026. Collectively, these amend the Revised School Code, specifically MCL 380.1303a, to require a school district's board of education to adopt a policy prohibiting students from using a wireless communications device during instructional time, effective for the 2026-27 school year. The update revises Miller Johnson's existing policy to comply with MCL 380.1303a and to use language consistent with the statute. Miller Johnson's related guidance is titled "New Law Prohibits Students from Using Wireless Communication Devices - Effective 2026-2027 School Year."

The retitled Wireless Communication Devices section (replacing "Personal Electronic Devices") reserves the district's right to prohibit possession or use of wireless communication devices on district property or at district-related functions. "Wireless communication device" is defined as an electronic device capable of, but not limited to, text messaging, voice communication, entertainment, navigation, accessing the internet, sending and receiving photos and videos, or producing email, replacing the prior definition of a privately owned device used for audio, video, or text communications including cell phones, personal laptops, smartwatches, smart glasses, and other wireless device connections. "Instructional time" means time that any student is assigned to engage in learning and curricular activities by instructional staff. "School grounds" means a building, playing field, or property used for school purposes to impart instruction to students or used for functions and events sponsored by a school. The Superintendent may develop administrative regulations consistent with the policy.

Under the Prohibition of Wireless Communication Devices heading (replacing "Away-for-the-Day Requirements"), and in accordance with MCL 380.1303a, students are prohibited from using wireless communication devices on school grounds unless required by law. The prohibition is enforced by instructional staff through monitoring students during instructional time and the school day. Devices must be turned off and kept out of sight in lockers or cubbies.

Exemptions permitted by law allow students to use a wireless communication device during instructional time and the school day for medically necessary devices; district owned or issued devices under building staff discretion; devices used for instructional purposes with building staff discretion; devices used for special education programming and/or as an accommodation under a Section 504 Plan, Individualized Education Program, or the Americans with Disabilities Act; devices used for lesson-specific academic assignments at building staff discretion; and devices used in emergency situations as described in the School District's Emergency Operations Plan, where applicable per the plan, pursuant to MCL 380.1308b.

Under Recording and Broadcast, students may not use wireless communication devices to broadcast or record audio, images, or video of any student, staff member, or other person in the school or while attending a school-related activity unless the student has received permission from the person or persons to be broadcast or recorded. The prohibition does not apply to curricular or extra-curricular activities for which personal recording is generally permitted, such as athletic events and arts performances.

**Update 22.04 - Policy 3003, Instruction (Curriculum and Instruction - 3000 Series)**
The fiscal year 2026 State School Aid Act includes MCL 388.1764k, which provides additional requirements for school districts and intermediate school districts when an evidence-based curriculum for grades K-5 is not used per MCL 380.1280f. Adoption of the revisions is recommended for Section 164k compliance, with reference again to the Miller Johnson guidance documents "New Compliance Requirements Under Section 164k - State School Aid Act (FY 2025-2026)" and "Additional Guidance on Section 164k Compliance - District Surveys & Curriculum Requirements." The revised policy states that, to the extent feasible, student instruction will be delivered using research-based and peer-reviewed instructional methodologies, and that in compliance with MCL 388.1764k the School District will notify parents if the District uses a curriculum not on the state's evidence-based list per MCL 380.1280f for grades K-5 by September 30, 2026. The Superintendent may develop regulations consistent with the policy.

**Update 22.05 - Policy 5003, Purchasing (Business - 5000 Series)**
This revision corrects a minor spelling/grammatical error. Under State/Federal Grants and Awards, the Superintendent will promulgate legally compliant administrative regulations concerning expenditures of funds received through state/federal grants and awards, and shall establish and maintain effective internal control over financial grants and awards providing reasonable assurance that the program and funds are managed in compliance with applicable statutes (correcting "statuses"), regulations, and the terms and conditions of the awards.

**Update 22.06 - Policy 6013, Facility Dog (Facilities and Operations - 6000 Series)**
The update provides clarity to the definition of a "facility dog," and the policy should be used for school district owned dogs. The revised text defines facility dogs as School District owned dogs trained to work within school facilities and at school events with children with a variety of academic, social, and emotional needs. The Superintendent will promulgate an administrative regulation applicable to the use of Facility Dogs on School District property.

**Update 22.07 - Policy 7001, Goal (School and Community Relations - 7000 Series)**
The update adds a Record Retention section. The School District will retain all public records in accordance with the Michigan Department of Technology, Management & Budget retention schedule for school districts. Unless the District is in receipt of a litigation hold or similar notice, records may be disposed of after the retention period in accordance with the state schedule.

**Update 22.08 - Policy 7008, Advertising (School and Community Relations - 7000 Series)**
The revision provides school districts more flexibility in preparing regulations to consider accepting advertisements generally. No advertising may be distributed, posted, or displayed on or within any District-owned property without the written consent of the Superintendent. The Superintendent shall prepare regulations addressing the circumstances under which the District would consider accepting advertisements, including but not limited to commercial advertisements.

**Update 22.09 - Policy 8003, Website and Digital Content Accessibility (General Policies - 8000 Series)**
The policy title changes from "Web" to "Website and Digital Content Accessibility." The revisions ensure compliance with the WCAG 2.1 Level AA ("WCAG") standard per recently updated requirements of the U.S. Department of Justice, with Miller Johnson guidance titled "New ADA Rules for District Websites & Apps." Under General, the School District is committed to ensuring that its website, online platforms, and mobile applications are accessible for students, parents, employees and members of the public. All pages on the District's website, online platforms, and mobile applications will conform to the W3C WAI's Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1, Level AA conformance, or any updated equivalent standard. The School District will continue to evaluate and test future releases and updates of its website, online platforms, and mobile applications and remains committed to maintaining ongoing compliance and serving the widest possible audience. To support this commitment, the District will conduct periodic accessibility audits of its website, online platforms, and mobile applications.
